subject: RE: Fantastico's Mexican Food – Signage Research Follow-Up (06/15/26)
body:
Good afternoon,

 

I’ve been looking into this and talking with our Director of Community Development. It seems that the freeway pylon sign could be Legal non-conforming, and as such, we would likely allow signage in the existing cabinet. As for Electronic Message Center signs, we would likely allow this, so long as it meets the requirements in Eloy City Code - 21-4-3.9 C. 

 

I’m not able to say for sure if something would be approved or not until a formal submittal is made, but if you are just looking to insert an EMC into the existing cabinet with little to no modifications to the existing structure, it is reasonable that the city would support that. If you need to start making more intensive improvements to the existing structure then there may be additional considerations that need to be addressed. If for some reason the existing structure would need to be replaced or heavily modified, it’s reasonable to believe that it would lose it’s legal non-conforming status and would need to be brought up to current sign standards, which would not allow for a freeway pylon sign.

 

Let me know if you have any other questions.
Sam

 

 

 

 

Some notes to keep in mind:

 

City Sign Code: https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-9920 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-9920> 

 

21-8-4.3: LOSS OF NONCONFORMING STATUS:

If a nonconforming use of land or a nonconforming use of a conforming structure is discontinued for a continuous period of six (6) months, the rights to a legal nonconforming status shall terminate. The initial decision as to whether a prior existing, non-conforming use has been abandoned shall be made by the Zoning Administrator. Such decision may be appealed to the Board of Adjustment by the affected property owner within ninety (90) calendar days of the ruling by the Zoning Administrator following the procedures under section 21-6-11.8 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-11111#JD_21-6-11.8> , "Appeal", of this chapter. (Ord. 18-880, 7-23-2018)

 

 

  21-4-3.9 - C.   Electronic Message Center: Electronic message center (EMC) signs are permitted as identified in section 21-4-3.8 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-10023#JD_21-4-3.8> , table 4.3-1 of this section 21-4-3 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-9920#JD_21-4-3> , subject to the conditions identified below:

      1.   EMC signs shall be counted as a portion of the total aggregate sign area.

      2.   Signs must be entirely located on-site.

      3.   There shall be no moving or flashing green or red features that could be mistaken as traffic control devices.

      4.   Digital message portion of the sign shall not exceed fifty percent (50%) of sign area.

      5.   Sign shall be installed at least one hundred fifty feet (150') from a designated crosswalk.

      6.   Sign shall not be installed within three hundred fifty feet (350') of a residential structure.

      7.   EMC signs shall be separated from other EMC signs by a minimum of one thousand feet (1,000').

      8.   All continuous loop image progression occurring on the face or copy of the sign must have a minimum interval time of eight (8) seconds.

      9.   All EMC signs shall have automatic dimming controls, either by photocell (hardwired) or via software settings, to reduce the illumination intensity of the sign as ambient lighting conditions change.

 

G.   Freeway Pylon Signs: Freeway pylon signs are permitted as identified in section 21-4-3.8 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-10023#JD_21-4-3.8> , table 4.3-1 of this section 21-4-3 <https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/eloyaz/latest/eloy_az/0-0-0-9920#JD_21-4-3> , subject to the conditions identified below:

      1.   All freeway pylon signs shall be part of a comprehensive sign package that requires both review and recommendation by Planning and Zoning Commission and approval by the City Council.

      2.   Freeway pylon signs shall be counted as a portion of the total aggregate sign area.

      3.   One freestanding pylon sign shall be allowed per property; additional signs are allowed on a property with street frontage that exceeds two hundred feet (200'). If multiple signs are placed on a single street frontage, there shall be a minimum of one hundred feet (100') between each sign.

      4.   A freestanding pylon identification sign may be placed on Commercially or Industrially zoned property that has a minimum of three hundred feet (300') of freeway frontage. In order to apply for a freeway pylon sign, the site, or combination of sites, must be at least twenty (20) acres in size and the sign should identify multiple tenants (a maximum of 4 tenants) or a combined minimum of two hundred thousand (200,000) square feet of office, retail, or manufacturing space.

      5.   Sign copy shall be limited to name and/or logo identification with approved directional information.

      6.   The pylon identification sign shall not exceed an overall height of eighty feet (80') above the natural grade of the site; has a maximum width of twelve feet (12'), or a maximum depth of four feet (4').

      7.   Pylon signs shall not be located closer than a distance equal to the height of the sign from the freeway right-of-way. A minimum separation distance of three hundred feet (300') shall be observed between any such freeway pylon signs located on the same side of the freeway.

      8.   A total maximum sign area of six hundred (600) square feet; with any one panel not exceeding one hundred fifty (150) square feet in area, plus the center identification.

      9.   Pylon signs may not be installed on a parcel, lot or development site that has an existing billboard or other prohibited sign.

      10.   Council, when considering the required comprehensive sign package, may vary restrictions pertaining to height, sign copy, and separation distance upon appropriate justification presented by the applicant, such as, but not limited to, identification of regional or community centers or conveying a civic or public interest message.

      11.   Sign supports shall consist of at least thirty percent (30%) of the total sign width; each single support shall consist of at least fifteen percent (15%) of the total sign width.

      12.   Signs shall be composed of a decorative base, support, and sign face.

subject: 1 Week Away: Live Cirrus Edge demo
body:
Hi Steve,




One week from today, we are hosting a live walkthrough of Cirrus Edge for sign shops. Cirrus generates inbound demand for signage and routes those leads directly to you through Edge. Cirrus Edge puts leads, quoting tools, and co-selling support in one place.




Tuesday June 23rd | 2:00pm EST | 45 minutes




If you have not registered yet, here is what you will see:




*	How to claim leads Cirrus marketing sends your way

*	How to build and send a branded quote in minutes, including AR visualization so your customer can see the sign before they buy

*	How to monitor every display you install and resolve most issues without rolling a truck

*	How Cirrus works alongside you to help close deals

We will have a sign shop partner on the call sharing how they use Edge in their business and we'll end with a live Q+A.

subject: Construction with no off season
body:
How big venues and stadiums build around event complexity.
 <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRX0HO2v1jo60exlOUmJctGr3_fAujlU86oPz0lSV7XZ1qoQtzoJiQhCruYSpSApLq-IQ=>  
DIGITAL BUILDER 
Managing construction in large, always-on venues is a challenge that goes far beyond schedules and scopes. These environments demand constant coordination, clear communication, and careful planning to keep projects moving without disrupting daily operations or the experience of the people using the space. When work happens alongside live events and public activity, even small decisions can have outsized impacts.

In this week’s newsletter, we build on that reality by looking at how teams navigate these high-stakes environments with a mix of collaboration and connected digital workflows. From using visual tools to align technical and non-technical stakeholders to keeping information accessible and up to date, the focus is on practical ways technology supports better decision-making where there’s little margin for error.
	
 	 
IN TODAY'S EDITION: 

*	What makes managing construction at Gillette Stadium so challenging is that the venue never really stops operating. Go behind the unique construction operations at the iconic venue <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYARWl6BMrESEA7JqPBcKzGL6EeYMEFBhkOPCckQFZcEofvsykRAthrOtoOanKGHxfu0=> .
*	How Populous is rethinking stadium design with modular, productized approaches <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYPlKBBdoFJZ7zcLFiZKK9bfaw_HYNJbfp-ZKX9-2A6l618CzevU1men_v0UbFs_F_IM=>  that deliver faster, more sustainable venues.
*	See how Autodesk is helping the Cleveland Browns design and deliver a next-generation stadium experience <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYFUTy5tnV7zPne5FJRSQvmS-j7s22QhUYsQhOv8SJWdjb7krn25QPd7B2w1mLPJ7jno=> .

 <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYARWl6BMrESEA7JqPBcKzGL6EeYMEFBhkOPCckQFZcEofvsykRAthrOtoOanKGHxfu0=>  
Managing Construction in One of the Most Complex Venues in Sports	 
At Autodesk’s Digital Builder podcast, we spend a lot of time talking about technology. And while this episode also dives deep into construction tech, it also covers a lot of the things that make construction human: communication, coordination, and the people keeping everything moving. On this episode, I sit down with Woody Benisek-Beal, Director of Construction at The Kraft Group, the company that owns and operates Gillette Stadium. Woody and I talk about what it takes to manage construction at the stadium, given that it never truly shuts down.
	
Tune in <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYARWl6BMrESEA7JqPBcKzGL6EeYMEFBhkOPCckQFZcEofvsykRAthrOtoOanKGHxfu0=>  	
 <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYPlKBBdoFJZ7zcLFiZKK9bfaw_HYNJbfp-ZKX9-2A6l618CzevU1men_v0UbFs_F_IM=>  
How Populous Is Innovating Venue Productization—with Stadium-Size Impact	 
What if stadiums were built more like products than one-off projects? In this story, Populous shares how applying industrialized construction and modular thinking is helping teams design venues that are faster to build, more cost-efficient, and better suited for long-term use. From reusable components to tighter collaboration with manufacturers, it’s a fresh approach to creating high-impact spaces with less waste.	 
Explore the story <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYPlKBBdoFJZ7zcLFiZKK9bfaw_HYNJbfp-ZKX9-2A6l618CzevU1men_v0UbFs_F_IM=>  	
 <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYFUTy5tnV7zPne5FJRSQvmS-j7s22QhUYsQhOv8SJWdjb7krn25QPd7B2w1mLPJ7jno=>  
Autodesk is the Official Design and Make Platform for the Cleveland Browns	 
Autodesk is partnering with the Cleveland Browns to help shape the next era of stadium design, one built on connected data, smarter collaboration, and more sustainable construction. As the team plans its new Huntington Bank Field, Autodesk Forma and integrated workflows will support faster decision-making, reduce waste, and create a more immersive experience for fans.	 
Go behind the partnership <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYFUTy5tnV7zPne5FJRSQvmS-j7s22QhUYsQhOv8SJWdjb7krn25QPd7B2w1mLPJ7jno=>  	
Keep Digging 

*	See how Autodesk Forma Build and GCPay are connecting <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRX4NUXiTOuYT_-x7vnplN_n4z-GUXU62TV9MkFVx9FisxJtFHXfrM3b1Mlg_XlKqMTaI=>  field and finance to streamline cost management and payments.
*	It's time to rethink construction safety <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYCvon-ehH7pM0OwS1eg_0L1idm6zpcU7OXX5xIVuCfZQpul_woV6EgB1g_CTGBmW2dE=>  starting from the ground up.
*	Discover how data and AI are shaping a more connected and walkable vision for South Downtown Dallas <https://emconstruction.autodesk.com/NTcyLUpTVi03NzUAAAGidPMRYBXSfvfKvnc0tlKT-b0iDxT3nTvJLX4OXps-4ZuhM_t3UsKzLFqKDsEErLU_oYwOrD0=> .

body:
Ticket Status Notification

Ticket Information

Ticket Number: 2026061701163

Ticket Location: 3225 E GUADALUPE RD
GILBERT, MARICOPA, AZ United States
33.3642544818963, -111.721178469771 

Due Date: 06/19/2026 8:00 PM ET

Company: CHRISTY SIGNS

Phone: 6022424488

Fax/Email:  / STEVE@CHRISTYSIGNS.COM

 




Reason for Notification

Notification Type: Bore Standby        Date: 06/17/2026

You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path. 

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations. 

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a 

minimum of 2 hours prior. 

 480-730-3640

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path. 

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations. 

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a 

minimum of 2 hours prior. 

 480-730-3640

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. 	Hi Sarah,
	
	

	I hope you are doing well.

	
	I am reaching out regarding the First Watch project at Harvest Station (Permit No. B26-0143). We received the latest review comments and wanted to see if we could discuss the remaining Planning comment prior to preparing another resubmittal.

	
	The project has now been through several review cycles, and the current comment appears to relate to the Comprehensive Sign Plan requirements for the center, specifically the raceway mounting requirements noted on Sheet 4.

	
	Our concern is that we may continue revising and resubmitting without fully understanding the Town's expectations, which could result in additional review cycles and delays.

	
	The fabricator, project team, and customer have expressed interest in participating in a brief conference call if that would be helpful. Our goal would simply be to review the remaining comment, confirm what revisions are required for compliance with the Harvest Station CSP, and ensure the next submittal fully addresses the Town's concerns.

On Thu, Jun 18, 2026 at 2:47 PM Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com <mailto:steve@christysigns.com> > wrote:


	Hi Sarah,
	
	

	I hope you are doing well.

	
	I am reaching out regarding the First Watch project at Harvest Station (Permit No. B26-0143). We received the latest review comments and wanted to see if we could discuss the remaining Planning comment prior to preparing another resubmittal.

	
	The project has now been through several review cycles, and the current comment appears to relate to the Comprehensive Sign Plan requirements for the center, specifically the raceway mounting requirements noted on Sheet 4.

	
	Our concern is that we may continue revising and resubmitting without fully understanding the Town's expectations, which could result in additional review cycles and delays.

	
	The fabricator, project team, and customer have expressed interest in participating in a brief conference call if that would be helpful. Our goal would simply be to review the remaining comment, confirm what revisions are required for compliance with the Harvest Station CSP, and ensure the next submittal fully addresses the Town's concerns.

	
	Would you be the appropriate person to have that discussion with, or is there another reviewer we should coordinate with?

	
	Thank you for your time and assistance. We appreciate your help in moving the project toward approval.

	
	Best regards,

subject: Dig Safely Near Southwest Gas Pipelines
body:
DO NOT RESPOND TO THIS EMAIL. For any questions about your one call ticket, please contact your local call center.

STEVE SKYE,

THANK YOU for using 811 to submit a locate ticket for work near Southwest Gas pipelines. 

To help you avoid pipeline emergencies, follow these simple steps:

1.    Survey and mark your proposed dig area with white paint.

2.    Wait the required time. This is 2 working days, NOT including the date of notification.

3.    Respect the marks. Ensure all utility owners have responded before digging.  

4.   Contact Southwest Gas and request a monitor prior to bore operations or working within 10 ft. of high-pressure facilities. 

5.   Dig Carefully.  Watch this short video <https://www.swgas.com/en/excavator-safety?utm_source=link&utm_medium=website_email&utm_campaign=Damage_Prevention_Safe_Digging_Video&utm_id=Perseverant&utm_term=>  to learn best practices when digging around underground natural gas lines.

6.    Follow safe excavation laws for the state you're working in. 

Always dig with care! Damage to natural gas lines can result in costly repairs, service outages, and project downtime, as well as severe injury and/or death.  

To report a pipeline emergency or odor of natural gas, call 911 and Southwest Gas at 877-860-6020.

Thanks for working safely near our facilities.

Thank you for sending the revised Brand Book. 


Regarding the monument sign comment, I do not believe the city is necessarily stating that the monument sign is located within the right-of-way. My recommendation would be to revise the site plan to clearly identify:
• Property line and right-of-way line
• Monument sign location
• Setback dimension from the sign to the property line/right-of-way

Subject: Burger King #16449 – Pinal County Sign Criteria / Permit Requirements (05/06/26)

 



 

Hi Team,




I was able to speak with Valentyn from the Planning Department at Pinal County regarding the Burger King #16449 project and reviewed the applicable sign criteria associated with the 2006 CSP.




Based on our discussion, it appears the County is no longer requiring a separate Comprehensive Sign Plan review for this parcel.


Below are the primary items needed for the permit package and sign calculations:

*	Sign allowance is based on building frontage
*	Allowance calculation:

subject: Desert Palms center
body:
Warner Rd and Alma School.

 

Hello Steve!

 

I just talked again with our planner Darsy Smith (darsy.smith@chandleraz.gov <mailto:darsy.smith@chandleraz.gov> ) and she reiterated that the new shops parcels, which include your interested parties, has indeed submitted application for review with planning under the Desert Palms center name and will be considered, as it was originally, as part of this center and must follow the regulations provided as far as what signage will be allowed.

 

There is room for 2 more multi-tenant signs along Warner Rd (which should match the newly remodeled center signs with each at 8’ max ht) for the center and the new shops/restaurants. I have detailed this previously but let me or Darsy know if you have further questions. Darsy has already discussed with her Planning Manager who stated that no individual tenant signs will be permitted but as I have alluded to, there is options with manipulating the panel areas on the multi-tenant signs for larger panels for specific tenants per the property owner/management’s discretion. I hope this helps.

 

Have a great day!

Subject: First Watch – Queen Creek Review Comments (06/18/26)

 



 

Hi Joshua,




We have received the latest comments from the Town of Queen Creek (see attached).


At this point, it may be beneficial to arrange a conference call with Kimberly Pippin and/or Sarah Clark before preparing another revision package. The project has now gone through multiple review cycles, and the remaining comments appear to be related to interpretation of the Harvest Station Comprehensive Sign Plan rather than standard sign permit requirements.


My concern is that continued revisions without direct clarification from the reviewer may result in additional correction notices and further delays.


A brief discussion with the Town may help confirm exactly what they are expecting regarding the raceway requirements and any other CSP-specific criteria before another resubmittal is prepared.


Please let me know if you would like us to help coordinate that discussion with the Town.


Best regards,

subject: Re: Fantastico's Mexican Food – Preliminary Zoning Report (06/12/26)
body:
Currently we are in process of gettng an inspector 


	On Jun 12, 2026, at 13:52, Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com> wrote:
	
	

	﻿ 

	Hi Thomas,
	
	

	Attached is our preliminary zoning report for the Fantastico's Mexican Food property located at 4985 N Sunland Gin Road in Eloy.

	
	Our initial review indicates that the property is zoned C-2 General Commercial, which generally supports commercial tenant identification signage, including wall signs, monument signs, and illuminated signage. The report also summarizes the applicable sign ordinance provisions and permitting requirements identified during our research.

	
	At this stage, the report is intended to provide a preliminary overview of the zoning and sign regulations applicable to the site. The final allowable sign area has not yet been calculated and will require verification of the building frontage, street frontage, existing site signage, and any applicable setback conditions.

	
	Our next step will be to complete a detailed sign compliance analysis and determine the maximum allowable signage available for the property based on the City's frontage-based calculations.

	
	Please review the attached report and let me know if you have any questions. We will continue refining the analysis as additional site information becomes available.

	
	Thank you,

	 

	Steve Skye

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Thursday, Jun. 25, 2026

CONTACT:
Cindy Casaus, Assistant Director & Chief of Communications


AZ ROC: Scottsdale-Based Pool Contractor's License Revoked

PHOENIX, Ariz., (Jun. 25, 2026) - On Thursday, June 25, 2026, Arizona Registrar of Contractors (AZ ROC) revoked the KA-5 Dual Swimming Pool Contractor license held by Sun State Pools LLC (ROC 339772), a Scottsdale-based contracting business. 

AZ ROC received and began investigating 85 complaints from homeowners and subcontractors against Sun State Pools LLC received between September 9, 2025 and June 25, 2026. One case resulted in a citation issued on June 8, 2026 and required Sun State Pools LLC to file a written answer by June 24, 2026 which the company failed to do. After the company failed to answer the citation, the Registrar revoked the license effective June 25, 2026. 

AZ ROC continues to investigate the complaints it has received and strongly encourages any other impacted homeowners to file their complaints with the Agency as soon as possible. Following adjudication, those whose complaints result in discipline of the license are able to file a claim with AZ ROC’s Residential Contractors' Recovery Fund, which is available to homeowners after a contractor has been found to be in violation of Title 32, Chapter 10 of the Arizona Revised Statutes. 

The Fund can provide a maximum payout to each homeowner of up to $30,000, but the maximum amount available per residential license is $200,000. If all valid claims exceed the $200,000 per license limitation, the Registrar will pay claimants on a pro rata basis. In cases where there are numerous complainants, there is a possibility that the monies available in the Fund will be exhausted before all eligible homeowners submit a claim for a payout from the Fund. This is why it is crucial for homeowners to submit their complaints to AZ ROC right away. 

While hiring a licensed contractor does not guarantee a problem-free project, hiring licensed contractors does provide a pathway to access AZ ROC’s administrative process in order to have work corrected or completed. The Agency has a two-year jurisdiction from the date of occupancy or date when the last work was performed to investigate complaints if the workmanship is below standard or is in violation of existing codes. There is no recourse through AZ ROC if the business hired to perform the work is unlicensed. Always check the license by visiting roc.az.gov <https://click-1617733.icptrack.com/icp/relay.php?r=37004434&msgid=247161&act=6394&c=1617733&pid=623354&destination=http%3A%2F%2Froc.az.gov%3Futm_source%3DiContact%26utm_medium%3Demail%26utm_campaign%3Dcindy-casaus-assistant-director%26utm_content%3DAZ%2BROC%253A%2BScottsdale-Based%2BPool%2BContractor%25E2%2580%2599s%2BLicense&cf=11519&v=fb91b27f5553a7b2cf41d823fdfa4544aa819a74a44b8a6882ef5a77f0cb6104>  or by calling the Agency at (877) 692-9762.

Hi Rocky,

The City of Chandler has completed the first review of the Alma Park sign permit application and has issued correction comments. Overall, the comments are straightforward and primarily require revisions to the drawings rather than redesign of the signs.


The city is requesting the following updates before the application can be resubmitted:

*	Engineering: Provide sealed structural details for each monument sign prepared by a Structural or Civil Engineer. We can use the ASA engineering worksheet if desired. 
*	Electrical Information: Expand the electrical notes to fully comply with 2024 IBC / 2023 NEC Article 600. The plans should identify: 

	*	Source electrical panel and panel designation. 
	*	Dedicated 120V, 20A branch circuit. 
	*	Conductor type and size. 
	*	Conduit type, size, and burial depth. 
	*	External lockable disconnect switch located within sight of the sign. 
	*	Equipment grounding and bonding per NEC Article 600. 
	*	UL-listed sign components and installation in accordance with NEC Article 600 and local electrical codes. 

*	Tenant Panel Construction: Revise the specifications to state that all illuminated tenant panels are routed with 1/2-inch push-thru acrylic rather than "back-up acrylic." All three monument signs should use identical construction terminology and matching fabrication criteria.
*	Panel Color: Note the background color for the tenant panels and indicate that all tenant panels will have matching background colors
*	Site Plan: Provide a revised site detail showing: 

	*	Exact monument sign location. 
	*	Setback from the back of curb. 
	*	Distances to the nearest property lines and right-of-way. 
	*	Required visibility triangles demonstrating the sign does not obstruct vehicular sight distance. 

This shopping center may have a Comprehensive Sign Program (CSP), I have called the City of Chandler sign department to check if this is the case. 


Once these revisions are completed, we can upload the revised plans for the next review cycle.


Regards,

Subject: [External] Stotz Equipment #074063 – Survey Exhibit Request (07/01/26)

 

	CAUTION: This email originated from outside of Pattison ID. Exercise caution when clicking links or opening attachments and verify the sender's identity and the content's safety before proceeding. 

 

Hi Chris,

It was nice meeting with you and the Pattison ID team to review the status of the Stotz Equipment project.


As we discussed, we'd like to proceed with having a stamped survey exhibit prepared to assist with the Maricopa County permit review. This appears to be the best way to accurately document the property boundaries, easements, right-of-way information, and other site conditions necessary to establish a compliant location for the proposed monument sign.


Once the exhibit is complete, we'll place the proposed monument sign location on the survey so it can be shown relative to the property lines, easements, existing and future right-of-way, and any other applicable site constraints.


For your reference, I've attached the project notes, our right-of-way assessment, and the County-marked site plan that were discussed during the review. These documents summarize the outstanding permit comments and the MCDOT right-of-way requirements that need to be addressed.

When you have an opportunity, please let us know if you need any additional information to prepare the survey exhibit.


Thank you, and we look forward to working with you on this project.

 

Steve Skye

We’re excited to introduce the Signtag AI Chatbot, a website assistant built specifically for commercial sign companies.

Hi Taylor,

As I’ve been reviewing the previous email threads regarding the Habit Burger location in Surprise, I want to make sure I clearly understand what services Everbrite would like Christy Signs to provide before preparing a quote.


Based on the correspondence with the Prasada DRC consultant, it appears that two separate amendment reviews may be required:

• A Minor Building Amendment for the paint color change on the building elevation
• A Signage / Monumentation amendment to document the existing signage changes and murals


Following DRC approval, the City of Surprise may also require documentation through a sign permit or administrative clearance to reconcile the current building condition with the City’s permit record.


Because several parties appear to have been involved in preparing drawings and documentation (Lingl Design, Habit’s consultants, etc.), I want to confirm how Everbrite would like Christy Signs to participate in the process.


For example, would you like Christy Signs to:

• Prepare the amendment drawings and documentation
• Assemble and submit the DRC applications based on drawings provided by others
• Coordinate the City of Surprise permit or clearance process after DRC approval
• Or assist only with a portion of these steps


Once I understand the intended scope, I will be happy to prepare an estimate and outline the next steps.


Please let me know how you would like us to proceed.

subject: Re: Sales and Production Meeting
body:
Good morning!




I’ll be back on Monday.




I hope you all have a great meeting today!




As you review the install schedule, please work together to ensure we’re scheduling jobs that meet both our customers’ due dates and our weekly billing goal of $33,000.




Scott, after the meeting, would you please email me the install schedule along with the billing amount for each job and its due date?




Receivables:

Our expense accounts have been significantly impacted by lower receivables over the past several weeks. I understand we need to continue purchasing materials to keep production moving, and I’ll fund the accounts as soon as possible.




Billing:

Billing over the last three weeks has also been lower than we’d like. It’s important that we continue closing new jobs now so we can minimize the impact over the next 30–45 days.




I’m very pleased to report that since January we’ve steadily increased sales, improved our margins, and significantly reduced our past debt. Those are accomplishments everyone should be proud of.




We’re moving in the right direction, and I’m looking forward to getting back ahead of the game this month.




Have a great meeting and a great week!




Wendy

New FREE Payment Option!
Beginning February 22, 2025, customers can make development fee payments up to $2,000,000 using a new zero fee eCheck (ACH) payment method.


Credit card payments up to $75,000 will still be accepted, but the customer paid credit card service fee is increasing from 2.65% to 2.75%. 


Click Accela Citizen Access <https://aca-PROD.accela.com/GOODYEAR/default.aspx>  to access the record, view, and make payment.  Payment must be made in full prior to releasing the approved documents, plans, and permit.

Subject: RE: Sales Pipeline Update (07/08/26) 
 

Hi Wendy,



Thank you for reviewing these projects and outlining your concerns. I completely understand the need to manage our credit exposure.


After reviewing PSCO / ID Associates' payment history, I believe we've identified that the primary issue has been following their established accounts payable process. They require invoices to be sent directly to their accounting contact, Pat Chevrette, and their payment timeline begins when Accounting receives the invoice, not necessarily the invoice date.

From: Steve Skye <steve@christysigns.com>
Sent: Monday, 13 July 2026 09:39:00
To: Wendy Christensen <wendy@christysigns.com>
Cc: Rocky Marsh <rocky@christysigns.com>
Subject: Proposed Plan for PSCO / ID Associates Payment Terms (07/13/26) 
 

Hi Wendy,



Following your email concerning adjusting the terms for PSCO / ID Associates, I spoke with Pat Chevrette, their A/P Manager for better understand how they handle payment arrangements.


Pat explained that they are willing to work with vendors on payment terms, but these discussions are typically handled with the project manager before the purchase order is issued. Depending on the project, they can accommodate:

*	Net 30 terms (when approved) 
*	Deposits 
*	Upfront payment of permit fees 
*	Upfront payment of crane or other significant third-party costs 
*	Progress payments on larger projects 


Based on that conversation, here is my proposed plan:



Aaron's and Tractor Supply (Current Projects)

I will contact each project manager and request a progress payment to reimburse Christy Signs for costs already incurred, including permit fees and other project-related expenses. Pat explained that the project managers have the authority to approve special payment arrangements, and if they approve an interim payment, she will coordinate the payment through Accounts Payable.

If the project managers prefer to leave the existing payment terms unchanged, we will continue following their established A/P process by sending invoices directly to Pat and monitoring payment through completion.



Darr Equipment (Future Purchase Order)

Since the purchase order has not yet been issued, this is the appropriate time to discuss payment terms with the project manager before the PO is released. I will explain that Christy Signs would like to establish payment terms that work well for both companies and discuss options such as a deposit, progress payments, upfront payment of permit fees, crane costs, or other significant project expenses before the purchase order is finalized.

 

Going forward, I recommend that we make this part of our standard process for PSCO / ID Associates. Rather than automatically accepting their default 45-day terms, we should discuss and establish payment terms with the project manager before each purchase order is issued. This will help manage Christy Signs' credit exposure while maintaining a positive working relationship with the customer.


Please let me know if you would like me to modify this approach before I begin contacting the project managers.


Thank you,

 

Steve Skye

Hi Wendy,

Thank you for reviewing these projects and outlining your concerns. I completely understand the need to manage our credit exposure.


After reviewing PSCO / ID Associates' payment history, I believe we've identified that the primary issue has been following their established accounts payable process. They require invoices to be sent directly to their accounting contact, Pat Chevrette, and their payment timeline begins when Accounting receives the invoice, not necessarily the invoice date.


Since I began sending invoices directly to Pat and following up, payments have been received within their normal payment cycle (see attached). 


Because Aaron's and Tractor Supply were accepted under their existing terms, I think we should honor those commitments. Going forward, however, I agree it's appropriate to discuss improved payment terms or a higher credit limit for future projects. If those terms aren't possible, we can then decide whether future projects fit within Christy Signs' acceptable credit exposure.


Thank you,

subject: follow up of todays meeting
body:
Hi Steve,

I just want to tell you how pleased I am with you and the outcome of today’s meeting regarding terms for PSCO brands. 

I feel confident you will succeed in securing deposits and negotiating the terms. 

To recap: If you get 50% down , I prefer balance paid as: 25% in 15 and 25% in 30. 

However, if you get the 50% down you have the authority to waive the 15 day payment a long as the balance is net 30.

I’d like to see a copy of the PO tomorrow, please.

Doing good!

Thanks!

wendy

subject: RE: Coral Gables Estates – Preliminary Site Review Report (07/15/26)
body:
We do not have any drawing or renderings at this time, we are working on getting bids for the below items.           

Windows: replace all 3 sets of windows with new Vinyl framed glass, frames should be black or dark bronze inside and out, glass should be E90 tint or better, glass panels should slide side to side to open (not up and down), bug screens should be included, labor and installation should be included, list warranties on glass/frames/installation

 

Doors: replace both exterior doors with commercial grade glass doors with slim metal frames, frames should be black or dark bronze inside and out, door opening system that holds door open on a locked position with a pull close system, include insulated strips and door sweeps for complete fit

 

Exterior Stucco - a traditional ‘Santa Barbara flat finish’ on all exterior surfaces except for soffits.  Complete wall to wall, floor to ceiling coverage including wrapping corners and base of walls.  

 

Interior - remove interior door, frame and drywall leading to the back room (where the refrigerator is now) and remove existing decorative window in that back room, frame it out with drywall and stucco.  This will create one large continuous wall area for all of the mailboxes.  Move existing mailboxes to this area.  

 

Interior walls - new ‘flat smooth finish’ on top of all existing drywall (walls and ceiling), fully sanded to final ‘ready to paint’ finish

 

Interior flooring - remove toilet, remove all existing flooring down to smooth concrete subfloor, remove all existing baseboards, replace with ‘through body porcelain’ tiles size 24 x 24 or 24 x 28 and all new baseboards that have been primed. Install new standard size (elongated bowl and seat) white Kohler toilet.  Tile color and design TBD but should be in the family of Grey.

 

Cabinets - sand existing cabinets to base wood, either stain or paint cabinets (color TBD) and seal them.  Do not remove cabinets nor countertops.  

 

Interior lighting - remove both existing fluorescent light fixtures and replace with white Can lighting and LED daylight white bulbs, install 4 or 5 blade new ceiling fan, dark bronze or black  (hugging the ceiling, no drop rod) in the middle of the space. Basic fan such as Hunter or similar brand with a wall remote.

 

Roof - remove all existing tile.  Get quotes for 2 different options: 

1. Standing seam metal in matte black or dark bronze.  Add matching metal fascia for a finished look.

2. Flat profile concrete tile in dark charcoal or black. Add wood fascia for finished look. Check existing felt to ensure useful life. 

 

Exterior signs - remove existing wooden community name sign and ‘Stop’ sign.  Replace community sign with decorative metal script sign and replace stop sign with basic metal sign // suggested design formats welcome, should be modern with matte black or dark bronze lettering to compliment metal or flat profile roof and possibly with back lighting for the community name sign.

 

Paint - all exterior walls: white primer, white Sherwin Williams paint with semi-gloss finish.  Exterior columns: gray primer, matte black paint Sherwin Williams eggshell finish.  All Interior walls and ceiling: white primer white Sherwin Williams paint with satin finish.

Senior Community Manager / Transition Manager

Subject: Chandler Review Corrections – Chick-fil-A #2567 (04/13/26)

 

Hi Scott,

I wanted to bring to your attention the review comments issued by the City of Chandler Sign Department for the Chick-fil-A #2567 project (SGN26-0083).


The City has completed their initial review and provided corrections that will need to be addressed prior to permit approval.


At a high level:

• The site plan currently reflects a proposed layout that has not yet been approved by Planning. Because of this, the reviewer cannot approve the plan as submitted.
• The reviewer has marked certain ground signs to be omitted for now. They are requesting that we revise the plan set and resubmit without those signs so that the wall signs and remaining signage can be approved.
• Once Planning approves the overall site layout, a subsequent submittal will be required for the omitted ground signs.


Additionally:

• All drive-thru directional signs must be reduced to a maximum height of 3'-0" (36").
• Future resubmittals must clearly show all directional sign locations and confirm compliance with this height requirement.


In summary, we can proceed by revising the current plan set to remove the flagged signs and move forward with approval of the wall signage, while the ground signs will follow after Planning finalizes the site plan.


I’ve attached the full correction set for your review. Let me know how you’d like to proceed, and we can begin coordinating the revisions.


Best regards,

Steve Skye

Subject: Chandler Review Corrections – Chick-fil-A #2567 (04/13/26)

 

Hi Scott,

I wanted to bring to your attention the review comments issued by the City of Chandler Sign Department for the Chick-fil-A #2567 project (SGN26-0083).


The City has completed their initial review and provided corrections that will need to be addressed prior to permit approval.


At a high level:

• The site plan currently reflects a proposed layout that has not yet been approved by Planning. Because of this, the reviewer cannot approve the plan as submitted.
• The reviewer has marked certain ground signs to be omitted for now. They are requesting that we revise the plan set and resubmit without those signs so that the wall signs and remaining signage can be approved.
• Once Planning approves the overall site layout, a subsequent submittal will be required for the omitted ground signs.


Additionally:

• All drive-thru directional signs must be reduced to a maximum height of 3'-0" (36").
• Future resubmittals must clearly show all directional sign locations and confirm compliance with this height requirement.


In summary, we can proceed by revising the current plan set to remove the flagged signs and move forward with approval of the wall signage, while the ground signs will follow after Planning finalizes the site plan.


I’ve attached the full correction set for your review. Let me know how you’d like to proceed, and we can begin coordinating the revisions.

You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.

2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path.

3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations.

4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a

minimum of 2 hours prior.

 602-484-5085

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.
*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.
*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.
*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.
*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.
*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.
*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.




Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.
*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.
*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.
*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.
*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.
*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.
*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .






Favor de hacer llegar al excavador correspondiente.

		PROJECT: 2605070 - Chandler Fashion Center Pylon Sign - Chandler, AZ

		1. Preliminary Engineering for 75' Pylon on Sheet 1 (cast-in-place pier foundation & primary support pole only, does not include stamped engineering): $270
