		General Service Understandings  ← Updated January 2024: please familiarize yourself!

		1. The base deliverable is a digital set of structural drawings (11x17) and an accompanying set of structural calculations (8.5x11) produced by Reverence Engineering unless communicated otherwise.

		2. The base deliverable will be stamped and signed by an engineer appropriately licensed in the subject jurisdiction. Reverence Engineering does have partner engineers employed for specialty or small-volume jurisdictions; all work is performed and managed at Reverence Engineering, but the final stamp by the licensed engineer may read differently.

		3. The base deliverable shall convey the structural intent and basis for design conformance. The base deliverable is not a fabrication or shop-level set of drawings and will likely not include shop-level specificity and components not part of the structural system.

		4. All features under a project request will be provided in one package unless requested differently before commencing work or if already part of a pre-engineered program. Separating features into individual packages will incur an additional fee after work has commenced.

		5. Project estimates (when issued) are typical and based on information available at the time the estimate is issued. Estimates and services should be assumed to be consistent with standard industry service offerings for obtaining a permit. Special requests or requests above and beyond what is typical must be communicated.

		6. Project estimates are based on an expected level of effort, experience, and time across various internal functions using one standardized company rate. Specific billable rates and time per rate cannot be broken out.

		7. Project estimates do not include shipping, printing, additional copies, additional forms, shop reviews, or any other accessory services outside of the base deliverable unless specifically communicated.

		8. Estimated project timelines are typically based on the presumption that the proposed design concept is generally adequate and all necessary information is provided at the time of award. Inadequate design concepts (which may or may not be apparent until a certain level of analysis is performed) or incomplete information may require additional time to complete the service request and may require additional billable time should the scope need to materially change.

		9. Final service fees may vary with additions or changes that materially alter the work effort such as, but not limited to::

		a. Additional client or jurisdictional requirements

		b. Specific or atypical project requests or requirements

		c. Additional requests or information that materially alter the work effort

		d. Requests or information that creates rework

		e. Peer review or plan check comments

		f. Response Letters, forms, and other official correspondence

		g. Meetings and conferences not specifically requested by the engineer.

		10. The engineered design will match any provided shop-level or fabrication drawings as closely as possible where specific design information exists. Reverence Engineering will assume that provided specifications are purposeful and will not alter elements of the design unless code compliance, safety, or company standards dictate. Where specific information is not shown or otherwise provided, a reasonable engineered solution will be provided. 

		11. Official plan check comments other than those stemming directly from errors or omissions as they relate to the contracted scope of work are considered additional billable. 

		12. Reverence Engineering is not familiar with and does not research jurisdictional administrative requirements. Any administrative requirements affecting the base deliverable (such as formatting) must be communicated to Reverence Engineering. Additional fees may apply. 

		13. Reverence Engineering is not responsible for the accuracy of existing or field conditions. It is the responsibility of the client to provide all appropriate information for consideration in analysis and design development. Where information cannot be provided or verified, Reverence Engineering may make assumptions about the existing conditions for permitting purposes at the direction of the client. Such assumptions may not accurately represent actual field conditions and additional engineering services may be required to address site conditions at a later date.

		14. It is the responsibility of the fabricator and/or installer to verify all field conditions before procurement of parts and materials and before fabrication.

Should a jurisdiction require that client-produced drawings (ie, a brand book or art deck) be stamped for permitting purposes, Reverence Engineering must have already produced an independent base deliverable for each feature shown. Client-produced drawings must then be reviewed and reconciled to remove possible discrepancies. An additional fee will apply. Reverence Engineering will not modify documents produced by others; all modifications must be performed by the owner of such documentation.

I wanted to bring to your attention the review comments issued by the City of Chandler Sign Department for the Chick-fil-A #2567 project (SGN26-0083).


The City has completed their initial review and provided corrections that will need to be addressed prior to permit approval.


At a high level:

• The site plan currently reflects a proposed layout that has not yet been approved by Planning. Because of this, the reviewer cannot approve the plan as submitted.
• The reviewer has marked certain ground signs to be omitted for now. They are requesting that we revise the plan set and resubmit without those signs so that the wall signs and remaining signage can be approved.
• Once Planning approves the overall site layout, a subsequent submittal will be required for the omitted ground signs.


Additionally:

• All drive-thru directional signs must be reduced to a maximum height of 3'-0" (36").
• Future resubmittals must clearly show all directional sign locations and confirm compliance with this height requirement.


In summary, we can proceed by revising the current plan set to remove the flagged signs and move forward with approval of the wall signage, while the ground signs will follow after Planning finalizes the site plan.


I’ve attached the full correction set for your review. Let me know how you’d like to proceed, and we can begin coordinating the revisions.

subject: RE: Chick-fil-A & AZP Monument Sign Review (06/10/26)
body:
Steve, Rocky,

 

In case we don’t talk today, here is the summary.

 

Planning has been approached by all parties for this signage proposal, and they have stated several times that no individual tenant signage will be considered, only the multi-tenant signs that match the new remodeled versions (8’ max height).

 

We can approve 2 new multi-tenant signs in that span. Starting from the larger 14’ sign in between the carwash and Wendy’s, and moving west, we can do a new sign every 275’ (min), as there is exactly room for 2.

 

These signs must be approved and permitted as duplicates of the existing signs, BUT…..The tenant panels can be manipulated per the discretion of the PM to accommodate individual tenants requests. For example, the sign must be approved with 5 max panels per side, but if the PM wanted to allow one tenant, usually like a major or anchor tenant, to utilize the space or total area of 2 or 3 panels, then they can allow this. So then you would have the same sign and sign panel area but with one large panel and 2 smaller ones. Just an example. The only requirements are that the panel background colors must meet the sign criteria (white), no corporate-colored panels, only corporate colored copy and graphics…ROUTED AND PUSH-THRU.

 

I hope this makes sense! Except for being away from my desk occasionally, I am here until 4:50 today and back in tomorrow at 8am.

 

Thank you!

 

Joe Sauer

Site Development Inspector

City of Chandler

Development Services Department

480-782-3065

joseph.sauer@chandleraz.gov <mailto:joseph.sauer@chandleraz.gov> 

https://www.chandleraz.gov <https://www.chandleraz.gov/> 

 

How was my service today? 

Visit #CelebrateTeamChandler | City of Chandler (chandleraz.gov) <https://www.chandleraz.gov/government/city-managers-office/mission-vision-and-values/customer-connection/survey>  to take a quick survey.

Cc: Rocky Marsh <rocky@christysigns.com>

Hi Joe,

I hope you are doing well.


We are looking for some guidance regarding a proposed monument sign arrangement within the Desert Palms development at Alma School Road and Warner Road.


Attached is a site plan showing the proposed locations of:

• One Chick-fil-A monument sign
• One AZP multi-tenant monument sign


Based on the plan, the two proposed signs appear to be separated by approximately 302 feet. While this appears to satisfy the typical monument sign separation requirement, we are unsure whether the site's PAD zoning, Master Sign Program, or previously approved sign package would permit this arrangement.


Specifically, we are trying to determine whether Chandler would support:


A separate Chick-fil-A monument sign and a separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign located approximately 302 feet apart within the same overall development.


The parcels are anticipated to be separately owned, and we would appreciate any insight you can provide regarding whether this concept appears supportable or if Planning review would be required before moving forward.


Thank you for your time and assistance. Any guidance you can provide would be greatly appreciated.


Best regards,

From: Steve Skye 
Sent: Wednesday, June 10, 2026 11:57 AM
To: Rocky Marsh <rocky@christysigns.com <mailto:rocky@christysigns.com> >
Subject: RE: Chick-fil-A & AZP Monument Sign Review (06/10/26)

 

Hi Rocky,

I reviewed the Chandler Sign Code along with the site plan provided.


Based on the plan, the proposed Chick-fil-A monument sign and the AZP multi-tenant monument sign appear to be separated by approximately 302 feet, which would satisfy the 300-foot separation requirement typically applied to freestanding monument signs within commercial centers.


However, the primary issue does not appear to be the separation distance itself. The larger consideration is whether the site's PAD zoning and any previously approved sign package or Master Sign Program would permit the additional monument sign arrangement. The Chandler Sign Code indicates that PAD developments may be governed by previously approved sign criteria that can supersede the standard code provisions.


Because of this, I would not consider the layout automatically approved based solely on the Sign Code. The proposal appears supportable from a spacing standpoint, but final determination should come from the Planning Department after reviewing the parcel configuration, ownership structure, PAD approvals, and existing sign program for the site.


My recommendation is that we contact Chandler Planning and request confirmation that the proposed arrangement of a separate Chick-fil-A monument sign and a separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign would be acceptable under the current PAD approvals.


Please let me know if you would like me to reach out to the city and obtain their interpretation.


Best,

 

Steve Skye

Fax: 602-271-0433

Email: steve@christysigns.com <mailto:steve@christysigns.com>

I just talked again with our planner Darsy Smith (darsy.smith@chandleraz.gov <mailto:darsy.smith@chandleraz.gov> ) and she reiterated that the new shops parcels, which include your interested parties, has indeed submitted application for review with planning under the Desert Palms center name and will be considered, as it was originally, as part of this center and must follow the regulations provided as far as what signage will be allowed.

I have detailed this previously but let me or Darsy know if you have further questions. Darsy has already discussed with her Planning Manager who stated that no individual tenant signs will be permitted but as I have alluded to, there is options with manipulating the panel areas on the multi-tenant signs for larger panels for specific tenants per the property owner/management’s discretion. subject: Chandler Fashion Center – Contract Review Observations (06/01/26)
body:
Hi Wendy,


I reviewed the Macerich Construction Services Agreement for the Chandler Fashion Center freeway pylon project and wanted to provide a summary of several provisions that may warrant additional review prior to execution.

The primary items that stood out are as follows:


• Payment Terms
The agreement does not appear to follow the 50% / 50% payment structure shown on our estimate. Instead, payments are based on monthly progress billings, with the Owner retaining 10% of approved billings until final completion and closeout. This may have a significant impact on project cash flow, particularly during engineering, permitting, material procurement, and fabrication.


• Retention
The agreement provides for a 10% retention on progress payments. Based on the current contract value, this could result in approximately $40,000 being withheld until final completion and acceptance.


• Final Payment Requirements
Final payment is contingent upon completion of all work, punch list items, governmental approvals, warranties, lien releases, as-built drawings, and other closeout documentation. The agreement also allows additional time for processing final payment after these requirements have been satisfied.


• Fixed Price Contract
The agreement identifies the contract amount as a fixed and firm price. Material cost increases, labor escalation, and other market fluctuations do not appear to be grounds for price adjustment unless addressed through an approved change order.


• Change Orders
The agreement requires written authorization for changes affecting cost or schedule. Work performed outside the original scope without proper written approval may not be compensable.


• Permits, Inspections, and Governmental Fees
The agreement places responsibility for permits, inspections, licenses, and related approvals upon the contractor unless otherwise stated. Our proposal currently identifies City permit fees as additional costs billed at actual cost, and this item may warrant clarification.


• Indemnification / Hold Harmless
The agreement contains broad indemnification and hold harmless provisions requiring Christy Signs to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Macerich and various affiliated entities from claims, damages, losses, expenses, and attorney's fees arising from our work to the extent caused by Christy Signs or its subcontractors. These obligations survive project completion and represent one of the more significant risk-allocation provisions within the agreement.


• Mechanic's Liens and Claims
The agreement also requires the contractor to promptly address mechanic's liens or similar claims and may require reimbursement of related legal expenses and costs incurred by the Owner.


• Schedule Requirements
The agreement places significant emphasis on schedule compliance and completion deadlines. Delays and schedule modifications generally require formal documentation and approval.


• As-Built Documentation
The contractor is responsible for maintaining and providing complete as-built drawings and project closeout documentation as a condition of final payment.

Overall, the provisions that appear most significant from a project management and financial standpoint are the payment structure, retention requirements, fixed-price language, indemnification obligations, and contractor responsibility for permits and inspections.

I thought it would be worthwhile to bring these items to your attention before the agreement proceeds further for review and execution.

Best,
 
Steve Skye

Fax: 602-271-0433

Hi Rocky,
 
Here are the direct answers to your questions:
 
- Glendale code does **not** specify different square footages for “major tenant” vs “minor tenant.” Sign area is calculated based on each tenant’s linear feet of frontage (Section 35.4.311).  
- The code does **not** limit tenants to one sign per elevation.  
- Yes, four-sided pad buildings are generally allowed signage on multiple sides (especially those facing public streets or drive aisles). The allowable square footage is determined per qualifying frontage.
 
**Recommendation:**  
We should mirror the approach used in the **303 and Bethany CSP** sample the City provided. It simply states that all building-mounted signs will be reviewed and approved under the standard City of Glendale Sign Code (rather than locking in detailed major/minor rules inside the CSP).
 
I’m attaching the 303 sample for you to review. Would you like me to draft the Building Signs section for Stonehaven using this exact same clean method?
 
Let me know and I’ll send it immediately.

Subject: RE: Stonehaven Marketplace – Sign Code Research (05/29/26) 
 
Hi Rocky,
I reviewed the Glendale Sign Ordinance, the Stonehaven PAD documents, and the available site information for Stonehaven Marketplace (NEC 91st Avenue & Camelback Road).

A few key findings:
• The site is zoned PAD (Planned Area Development) and the Stonehaven PAD specifically references preparation of a Commercial Master Sign Plan (CMSP) for the commercial portion of the development (see attached).
• The Glendale Sign Ordinance establishes the overall sign limitations such as sign type, height, area, and quantity, but it does not appear to establish major tenant versus minor tenant panel standards or tenant hierarchy requirements.

Based on the Glendale Sign Ordinance:

Freestanding Monument Signs
• One monument sign is permitted per 200 linear feet of street frontage.
• The site has approximately:
*         995.9 LF along Camelback Road
*         890.4 LF along 91st Avenue
• Based on frontage, the site could support up to three monument signs per frontage (six total), although the current concept showing two monument signs per frontage (four total) appears to be a more practical and defensible approach.
• Maximum height: 14 feet.
• Maximum sign area: 110 square feet per sign (parcel exceeds 20 acres).

Directional Signs
• Directional signs are permitted.
• Maximum size: 6 square feet.
• Maximum height: 3 feet.
• The code does not appear to establish a maximum number of directional signs, but they should be limited to legitimate traffic circulation and wayfinding purposes.

Tenant Panels / Major vs. Minor Tenants
I have not found any code section that specifically establishes:
• Number of tenant panels per monument sign.
• Major tenant versus minor tenant classifications.
• Required panel sizes.
• Required tenant hierarchy.
• Tenant copy size requirements.
• Anchor tenant panel requirements.

My interpretation is that these standards are intended to be created through the Commercial Master Sign Plan itself. In other words, Glendale provides the overall monument sign envelope (quantity, height, and area), while the CMSP establishes how the tenant panels are organized and displayed.

For the narrative, I would recommend establishing:
• Major Tenant panel standards.
• Minor Tenant panel standards.
• Tenant panel sizing criteria.
• Tenant hierarchy and placement standards.
• Directional sign program.
• Consistent monument sign design standards for the center.

I have attached the research summary and supporting code analysis for reference.

Best,

subject: Jas Diesel – Permit Approved / Next Step (05/01/26)
body:
Hi Team,


I wanted to provide an update on the Jas Diesel project and outline our path forward.


The permit has now been approved by the City of Phoenix. The project has also been revised as shown in the updated artwork (attached).

As discussed, we will need to procure the fuel price changer units from the manufacturer (Optec), their cutsheet is attached for reference. This differs from the originally planned display and will require integration once received.

To keep the project moving and meet the customer’s timeline, we will proceed with installation of the sign structure and cabinets first, with the price changers to be installed later once delivered. The cabinets are complete, and the pole is already set in the footing onsite.

The customer has emphasized the need to begin advertising fuel pricing as soon as possible and is requesting installation by 05/23. In the interim, we may utilize the electronic message center in a static format or provide a temporary/manual pricing solution until the permanent price changers are installed.

Before scheduling the official City footing inspection, we need to complete an internal pre-inspection of the footing to confirm readiness.


Next Steps:
• Perform internal footing pre-inspection
• Schedule City of Phoenix footing inspection
• Proceed with cabinet installation
• Order Optec price changers (8–10 week lead time) 
• Coordinate temporary pricing solution if required

Please review and advise if there are any concerns before we move forward.

Best regards,
 
Steve Skye

I wanted to follow up regarding the NextCare Urgent Care location in Apache Junction and share our findings from the recent site evaluation (see attached report) .
While the original scope was to perform an LED retrofit and address the current outages, our field review identified a broader issue. In addition to the electrical failures (including multiple letter outages and failed transformers), the sign is also experiencing significant material degradation. The acrylic faces are cracked, the vinyl is deteriorating, and overall components are showing signs of age-related wear.
Because of this, proceeding with a retrofit alone would not provide a reliable long-term solution. Retrofitting LED into compromised letter faces would likely result in inconsistent illumination and continued failures, leading to additional service calls.
Based on these conditions, we recommend a combined approach:
• Remove the existing neon system
• Install a new LED illumination system
• Replace all letter faces with new acrylic and vinyl
This approach will restore proper illumination, improve overall durability, and bring the sign up to current standards.

Hi Rocky,


I reviewed the Comprehensive Sign Plan package and overall, it looks very good. I did notice a few items that should be addressed before we proceed with submittal.

1. Sheet 3 – Sign Area Calculation
The sign area calculations for Sign 9 appear to still reflect the previous dimensions.
On Sheet 5, Sign 9 is shown as:
*         9'-0" × 3'-7"
*         Actual Sign Area = 32.50 sq. ft.
However, on Sheet 3 the summary still states:
*         Sign 9 Area = 50.00 sq. ft.
*         Sign 10 Area = 63.00 sq. ft.
*         Sign 11 Area = 63.00 sq. ft.
*         Total = 113.00 EQ. FT.
The corrected calculation should be:
*         Sign 9 = 32.50 sq. ft.
*         Sign 10 = 63.00 sq. ft.
*         Sign 11 = 63.00 sq. ft.
*         Total = 158.50 sq. ft.
The elevation summary already reflects approximately 158 sq. ft. proposed signage, so it appears only the callout text on the left side of the sheet needs to be updated.

2. Sheet 5 – Sign Numbering
There is a minor drafting issue on Sheet 5 where the "Sign 9" callout appears twice adjacent to the U-Haul cabinet sign detail. One of those callouts should likely be removed.

3. Project Address
Throughout the sign package the project is identified as:
U-HAUL
115 W DUVAL MINE RD
GREEN VALLEY, ARIZONA 85614
However, the attached Pima County parcel records for APN 303-33-556C identify the situs address as:
19050 S Alpha Ave
Sahuarita, AZ 85614
(Postal City: Green Valley)
I am not sure why there is a discrepancy, but I was unable to locate the Duval Mine Road address within the Pima County Assessor records, while the Alpha Avenue address appears to be the official situs address associated with the parcel.
I recommend we revise the project address to 19050 S Alpha Ave, Sahuarita, AZ 85614. This is the situs address identified by the Pima County Assessor for Parcel 303-33-556C and is the address accepted by the Town of Sahuarita permitting portal. While 115 W Duval Mine Road may be a commonly used business address for the facility, using the parcel situs address should help avoid permitting issues and ensure consistency between the permit application, parcel records, and jurisdictional databases.

Other than these items, the package looks good and appears ready to move forward once the corrections are made.

Thanks,
 
 
Steve Skye

subject: Comprehensive Sign Plan and Sign Permit Review Process (06/15/26)
body:
Good afternoon, Larry,


Thank you for speaking with me previously concerning the U-Haul project in Green Valley.

We are evaluating the signage entitlement strategy for the proposed U-Haul facility in Green Valley and would appreciate your guidance regarding the review process.

Our understanding is that the site currently appears capable of supporting a code-compliant signage package within the standard sign area allowances. However, the owner is also considering a Comprehensive Sign Plan to request additional sign area and flexibility beyond the standard code allowances.

When speaking with Building Safety, we were advised that once a sign permit is approved, a Comprehensive Sign Plan may no longer be an option. We are wondering if this may have been a misunderstanding and would appreciate clarification from the Planning Division.

Specifically, is it permissible to pursue a phased approach whereby:
1.	A sign permit application is submitted and reviewed based upon signage that complies with the current code allowances; and
2.	A Comprehensive Sign Plan application is submitted concurrently or subsequently to seek approval of additional signage beyond those allowances.

In other words, would approval of a standard sign permit preclude the property owner from later pursuing a Comprehensive Sign Plan for additional signage, or can the two processes proceed independently provided that any additional signage is not installed until the CSP is approved?

We appreciate any guidance you can provide regarding the preferred process and sequencing for these applications.

Thank you for your time and assistance.

Best regards,
 
Steve Skye

Thank you for sending the revised Brand Book. 

Regarding the monument sign comment, I do not believe the city is necessarily stating that the monument sign is located within the right-of-way. Without that information, Planning cannot confirm compliance and has therefore issued the comment that no signs are permitted within the public right-of-way.

My recommendation would be to revise the site plan to clearly identify:
• Property line and right-of-way line
• Monument sign location
• Setback dimension from the sign to the property line/right-of-way

subject: U-Haul Maricopa – Comprehensive Sign Plan Review Summary (07/15/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,

The Town of Maricopa has completed its first review of the proposed Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP). Overall, the reviewer appears supportive of processing the CSP but has identified several items that will require revisions before approval. The comments primarily focus on reducing the amount of signage proposed, modifying illumination adjacent to residential uses, and improving the monument sign design.

Below is a summary of the review comments and the applicable code provisions.


1. Aggregate Sign Area
The reviewer determined that the proposed sign package is significantly larger than can be approved.
The review notes that the total aggregate signage proposed cannot exceed 150% of the aggregate signage otherwise permitted by the zoning code, and further states that the maximum aggregate sign area for each building on separate lots is 150 square feet.
I reviewed the Maricopa Sign Ordinance and was unable to locate the 150% limitation within Chapter 18.115. The ordinance establishes the base sign allowances for commercial properties and allows Comprehensive Sign Plans to deviate from those standards when justified through superior architectural integration and design, but it does not expressly state a 150% cap. This appears to be an administrative policy or interpretation being applied by the Planning Department rather than language contained directly within the ordinance.

2. North Elevation Illumination
The reviewer notes that all illuminated signage facing Honeycutt Road must be revised.
This comment is supported directly by Maricopa City Code §18.115.070(F), which states:
"Signs directly facing residential districts shall not be illuminated."
Since the north elevations face the residential neighborhood across Honeycutt Road, those cabinet signs will need to be converted to non-illuminated versions.

3. Monument Sign
The reviewer is requesting that the proposed monument sign receive greater architectural treatment, specifically enhancing both the monument base and the sign structure itself.
The review also reminds us that monument sign height is measured from grade. Under §18.115.090(C), freestanding monument signs in commercial districts are limited to 6 feet in height, and §18.115.060(B)(1) specifies that height is measured from the adjacent curb or street grade to the highest point of the sign, including the monument base.
The ordinance also indicates that Comprehensive Sign Plans should promote superior architectural integration with the site and surrounding development, which appears to be the basis for the request to provide additional architectural interest.

4. Remaining Plan Sheets
The comments on the individual building elevations (Pages 6 through 10 and Page 12) simply reference the primary comments above and request that the plans be revised accordingly. No additional project-specific comments were provided for those sheets.

5. Property Owner Authorization
The Property Owner Approval Letter will need to be revised to include the printed name and title of the individual signing the authorization.

Overall, I believe the project remains in good standing. The comments do not suggest opposition to the Comprehensive Sign Plan itself but rather indicate that the City expects the proposal to better align with its sign regulations and design objectives. The largest design effort will be reducing the overall sign area, eliminating illumination on the north-facing elevations, redesigning the monument sign to provide a stronger architectural presence while remaining within the 6-foot height limit, and updating the owner authorization letter.

Please let me know if you'd like me to discuss any of these comments in more detail or review a revised CSP package before resubmittal.

Best,
 
Steve Skye
